issues.t: Sudden loss of drive power from inverter fault (recall 24V-832)
issues.sym: The truck suddenly stops pulling while driving and a message on the screen tells you to pull over and call roadside assistance. There is usually no warning beforehand.
issues.why: A drive inverter (the unit that turns battery power into motor power) on some trucks built from November 2023 to July 2024 can fail and stop sending torque to the wheels.
issues.next: Check your VIN on Tesla's recall page. Tesla replaces the inverter for free. If power cuts out, steer to a safe spot, put on the hazards and call Tesla Roadside.

issues.t: Stainless cant rail and light bar panel can come off (recall 25V-170)
issues.sym: The long stainless trim panel above the windshield and along the roof edge loosens, rattles or flies off while driving.
issues.why: The panel and built-in light bar are held on with adhesive that can let go (delaminate) over time, especially with heat, wind and car washes.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall and book the free cant rail replacement. Parts have been slow to arrive, so if the panel moves, tape it down and avoid highway speeds until it's fixed.

issues.t: Accelerator pedal pad can slip off and jam (recall 24V-276)
issues.sym: The pedal feels wrong or the pad on top of the accelerator moves. In the worst case the pedal sticks down and the truck keeps speeding up.
issues.why: On early trucks the pad on the accelerator pedal could work loose and get trapped by the surrounding interior trim, holding the pedal down.
issues.next: If the pedal ever sticks, press the brake firmly and shift to neutral. Check the VIN; Tesla repairs or replaces the pedal assembly for free.

issues.t: Giant windshield wiper suddenly stops working (recall 24V-456)
issues.sym: The single large front wiper stops moving, sometimes in the middle of a rainstorm, leaving you unable to see clearly.
issues.why: Too much electrical current can damage the wiper motor's controller, which kills the motor.
issues.next: Pull over safely if the wiper dies in rain. Check the VIN and get the free wiper motor replacement. Some owners say a replacement motor also failed, so report repeat failures.

issues.t: Wheel stud can break from cracked brake rotor (recall 26V-255)
issues.sym: Often no early sign. If a wheel stud breaks you may hear a knock or feel a vibration from one wheel. Mainly affects trucks with the 18-inch steel wheels.
issues.why: The holes in the brake rotor that the wheel studs pass through can crack, which can let a stud separate from the hub.
issues.next: Check the VIN. Tesla replaces the front and rear rotors, hubs and lug nuts for free. Stop driving and call for a tow if a wheel feels loose or knocks.

issues.t: Bed sail trim panel can blow off (recall 24V-457)
issues.sym: The large trim piece on top of the bed side (the sail) lifts, flaps in the wind or falls off. You may lose the outside tailgate and tonneau buttons that sit on it.
issues.why: The trim was stuck on with adhesive that wasn't applied properly on many early trucks.
issues.next: Check the VIN and book the free repair, where Tesla re-sticks or replaces the trim. Until then, use the screen or app for the tailgate and bed cover.

issues.t: Service-installed off-road light bar can loosen (recall 25V-735)
issues.sym: The accessory light bar mounted at the top of the windshield works loose, shifts or detaches, sometimes even at low speed.
issues.why: Some light bars fitted by Tesla service were attached using the wrong primer, so the adhesive doesn't hold.
issues.next: If your truck has the off-road light bar, check the VIN. Tesla inspects it and adds a mechanical fastening or replaces the bar for free.

issues.t: Truck won't drive soon after delivery (low-voltage system fault)
issues.sym: A 'pull over' or 'critical error' alert appears, the truck stops, stays stuck in Park or won't restart, and the screen may go black and beep.
issues.why: Early trucks had failures in the low-voltage electrical system that runs the computers, doors and controls. Without it, the truck can't shift or drive.
issues.next: Call Tesla Roadside; the truck usually has to be towed. This is a warranty repair. Note that doors open electrically, so learn where the manual door releases are.

issues.t: 'Critical steering issue' warning and limp mode
issues.sym: A red alert says a critical steering issue was detected and to pull over. Steering may feel different, and the truck may limit speed or refuse to drive.
issues.why: The Cybertruck uses steer-by-wire and rear-wheel steering run by electronics. A fault in those systems, sometimes with other electrical faults, triggers the alert.
issues.next: Pull over safely and don't keep driving. Contact Tesla Service; steering faults are covered by warranty and the truck often needs a tow.

issues.t: High-voltage battery fault or won't charge
issues.sym: Charging stops early or won't start at all, a battery error appears on the screen, or a charging alert blocks home charging.
issues.why: A fault inside the high-voltage battery pack or its wiring. Owners have reported moisture in the pack and high-voltage harness problems; some trucks needed a new pack.
issues.next: Don't keep retrying a charge that fails. Book service right away; the pack is covered by Tesla's battery warranty. Get any warranty denial in writing.

issues.t: Windshield cracks with no clear impact
issues.sym: A loud pop while driving, or a long crack across the huge windshield, sometimes when the defroster is on or on a cold morning in sun.
issues.why: The very large, steeply angled glass may be under stress in its frame, and temperature changes can start a crack. Small stone hits can also spread.
issues.next: Photograph the crack and ask Tesla whether it's a warranty claim. Check your insurance, which may cover glass. Use Tesla or a shop that can recalibrate the cameras afterward.

issues.t: Tires wear out very fast
issues.sym: Tread wears down far sooner than expected, sometimes in 6,000 to 20,000 miles, often unevenly on the edges.
issues.why: The truck is very heavy and has huge torque, so tires wear fast, especially with hard launches. Wrong alignment or pressure makes it worse.
issues.next: Check tread depth monthly and rotate every 6,250 miles as Tesla recommends. Get an alignment if wear is uneven, and use Chill mode for daily driving.

issues.t: Orange rust spots on the stainless body
issues.sym: Small orange or brown specks and stains appear on the stainless steel panels, often within weeks of delivery.
issues.why: The bare stainless has no clear coat. Iron dust from rail lines and brakes, road salt, tar and bird droppings sit on the surface and leave rust-colored stains.
issues.next: Wash the truck regularly and remove contaminants quickly. Tesla's manual suggests denatured alcohol for stubborn spots, then rinsing with mild soap. A clear wrap protects it.

issues.t: Driver-assist brakes hard or drifts in lane
issues.sym: With Autopilot or Full Self-Driving on, the truck brakes hard for no reason, drifts toward a lane line, or alerts that emergency braking is unavailable.
issues.why: The camera-based driver-assist system can misread the road, shadows or other cars. Dirty cameras and software changes affect it.
issues.next: Keep hands on the wheel and be ready to take over. Clean the cameras often, keep software updated, and report events to Tesla and NHTSA.

issues.t: Rear camera picture slow to appear (recall 24V-718)
issues.sym: After shifting into Reverse, the backup camera image shows up late, so you can't see behind you right away.
issues.why: A software problem delays the rear camera image beyond the federal time limit.
issues.next: Make sure the truck has the latest software. Tesla fixed it with a free over-the-air update. Look around before backing up.

issues.t: Low tire pressure light may turn off too soon (recall 24V-935)
issues.sym: The tire pressure warning comes on, then doesn't stay on after the truck is restarted, even though a tire is still low.
issues.why: A software error in the tire pressure monitoring logic.
issues.next: Install the over-the-air update. Check tire pressures with a gauge whenever the light has come on.

issues.t: Brake and ABS warning letters too small (recall 24V-051)
issues.sym: The brake, park and ABS warning symbols on the screen are smaller than the law requires and can be hard to read.
issues.why: The display software used the wrong font size for these warnings.
issues.next: Nothing to fix by hand; it was corrected for free by an over-the-air update. Make sure your software is current.

issues.t: Front parking lights too bright (recall 25V-699)
issues.sym: Other drivers may notice glare from the front parking lights.
issues.why: Software older than version 2025.38.3 drives the front parking lights brighter than federal rules allow.
issues.next: Install the latest over-the-air update, which corrects the brightness for free.

issues.t: Aero wheel covers rub the tire sidewalls
issues.sym: Rubbing or scuff marks on the tire sidewalls from the plastic aero wheel covers.
issues.why: The plastic covers can sit tight against the tire and wear into the rubber, which may weaken the sidewall over time.
issues.next: Inspect the sidewalls. If you see rubbing, remove the covers and have the tires checked; many owners drive without them.

issues.t: Door controller fault: window drops or door shows open
issues.sym: A door window lowers by itself, the door shows as open on the screen, or the door won't latch properly.
issues.why: The doors are electronic. A failed door controller or a poorly installed latch on early trucks causes the faults.
issues.next: Book service under warranty. Learn the manual door release in case the electronic opener stops working.

issues.t: Air suspension won't raise or lower
issues.sym: An 'adaptive ride control degraded' alert, or the truck won't change ride height when you ask it to.
issues.why: A fault in the adaptive air suspension (air springs, compressor or its controls).
issues.next: Avoid off-road use and heavy loads until checked, and book service under warranty.
